content: UX feedback (from dogfooding this repo directly): calling check_drift then scan_project as separate raw tool calls left the user with a stale/drift result and, after scanning, no guidance on what to do with the open_questions/diff — they had to know to ask an agent to interview them and write docs. Decision (user chose "extend start_documentation" over "add a separate sync_documentation prompt", explicitly to keep one prompt to remember instead of two): start_documentation now opens with a drift check whenever ensure_ai_dir reports the repo was already scanned before (status "conformant" or "upgraded" — as opposed to "initialized" for a brand-new .ai/, which has nothing to diff against yet). If check_drift comes back stale, the agent must summarize changed_files and ask the user directly "N files changed — want me to rescan and update the docs now?" before calling scan_project; a "no" stops the flow with a reminder they can resume anytime. check_drift and scan_project were deliberately NOT merged into one tool — they have different costs/side effects (check_drift is a cheap read; scan_project mutates last_scan_sha and the cache file) and other flows may want to call check_drift alone. Implemented in src/prompts/startDocumentation.ts (step 2), covered by new assertions in test/start-documentation-prompt.test.ts checking for "check_drift"/"stale"/"rescan" in the instructions text.
